newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Volcano erupts off coast of Papua New Guinea.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Volcano erupts off coast of Papua New Guinea.

text.p: Papua New Guinea's emergency services on Thursday were monitoring a small offshore volcanic island, which is home to 7,000 people, after eruptions threw rock and lava into the sea, authorities said.
National Disaster and Emergency Services director general Leith Anderson said activity had subsided on Manam island, about 15 km (nine miles) off the northeast coast of Papua New Guinea.

But islanders living on the lower slopes of the volcanic island may have to be evacuated if the eruptions worsened, Anderson told Reuters. "We've got contingency plans to evacuate if we have to," he said.
Anderson said eruptions on Tuesday night and Wednesday had sent lava down the island's northeast slope almost to the ocean.

"There are three vents at the summit of the volcano and they all went off simultaneously which is most unusual," Anderson said. "It was even throwing rocks and lava out into the sea...which is nearly a mile away."
Anderson said a vulcanologist had been sent to monitor the volcano which last erupted in both 1991 and 1992.
Papua New Guinea is on the Pacifc's volcanic belt called the "Ring of Fire".

Rabaul, a port town located on New Britain island 800 kms (500 miles) northeast of the capital Port Moresby, was devastated in September 1994 when two volcanoes on either side of the town erupted, forcing the evacuation of 30,000 residents.
